Luckily I've worked at places with short facilities in my buildings, but this is often an issue for people whose workplaces don't have showers. 

There are various solutions: 
Tell your workplace to put in a shower (active employees are healthier and happier, plus they need fewer parking places!)

Get to work some other way and then run or bike home

Find a nearby gym that you can get a membership to and use their showers

<Your creative idea here>
...

If you can work it out to do a commute where you get exercise as part of it, you'll free up time compared with driving to and from work and then trying to exerciseb separately, and you'll feel better.  I've run or biked to work most days for the past 35 years.  E-bikes increase the distance at which this is practical for many.

If you're new to cycling and worried about cycling in traffic, I highly recommend the book "Effective Cycling" by John Forester.

reviewedPosts.author: jerryjliu0
reviewedPosts.text:
We wrote a 36-page ArXiv whitepaper on ExtractBench 🧑‍🔬 , our effort to create the most comprehensive, schema-guided, real-world document extraction benchmark.

It’s extremely detailed and covers everything from comparisons with related work on document extraction, to the dataset construction / how ground-truth is generated, to our experiments over 14+ extraction systems.

Here are some of the most salient points from the paper:
✅ The benchmark scores schema-guided extraction on real enterprise documents. Given input doc + schema and predicted output from an extractor, the benchmark measures value accuracy, grounding, tags for each “challenge”, and cost.
✅ Compared to other benchmarks, we have more schemas, more evaluation dimensions, and more data domain diversity
✅ The ground-truth is constructed according to 3 doc subtypes: real-docs use a model ensemble + human review, synthetic long lists have ground-truth by construction, and scanned forms also have human review incl. boxes
✅ Our three modes (LlamaParse cost-effective, agentic, and agentic plus) are at the Pareto frontier of accuracy and cost.

The full ArXiv paper is here: https://t.co/s5azzQV8zr

Our site: https://t.co/VapjcfKCc3

最近 a16z 写了一篇很有意思的 Computer Use Agent 现状调查。

一个很明显的变化是：「会不会用电脑」已经开始变成基础能力，现在拉开差距的是能不能稳定完成一整套工作。

按文章引用的数据，OSWorld-Verified 的最好成绩一年里从约 42% 涨到了 85%，甚至超过了人类基线。

但企业真正部署以后，最头疼的还是那些剩下的失败，例如怎么验证结果、处理异常、恢复任务、让人接管，以及记住一家公司真正的工作方式。

甚至有一家每月跑数百万次自动化任务的公司，负责人已经不太关心底层到底用了哪个模型。

所以当模型操作电脑本身逐渐变成通用能力，Agent 的价值会更多转移到 Harness、Context、验证和真实业务流程上。

这可能才是 Computer Use 从 Demo 走向真正生产力工具的开始。

文章链接：https://t.co/5X4YLNREry

Agent 每做完一个任务，为什么下一个相似任务还要重新摸索一遍？

浙大、美团等团队这篇 SkillRise，研究的是让 Agent 在不同任务之间持续积累技能。

它会把相关任务串成一个逐渐变难的序列。Agent 完成当前任务后，把成功经验、失败教训和可复用流程整理进 Skill Document，再带到后续任务继续使用。

更关键的是，Skill 的价值由后续任务来检验。

一条经验有没有用，不看它总结得多漂亮，而看它能不能真正提高下一次任务的表现。

在 Qwen3-4B 上，SkillRise 在 ALFWorld、WebShop 和 ScienceWorld 上都超过了现有基线。测试时，相似任务序列从 2 个增加到 6 个，成功率也从 83.6% 提升到 87.5%。

这篇工作努力让 Agent 的经验开始真正跨任务流动。

能复盘一次经历还不够。

能把这次经历变成以后反复受用的技能，才更接近真正的学习。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/r71ljDrrJW

推荐一个很有意思的项目：Codex Router。

如果你喜欢 Codex 的工作流，但又想在里面直接用 Claude、Kimi、DeepSeek、Grok、GLM、Qwen 等模型，这个项目很值得试试。

它会把外部模型直接接进 Codex 原生的模型选择器里，和 GPT 模型放在一起。Codex 原来的 Commands、MCP、Skills 和任务状态都可以继续用，部分外部模型还可以直接作为 subagent。

类似 Claude Code Router、9Router 的项目已经不少，但它们更偏通用模型网关。Codex Router 做得更深的一点，是专门围绕 Codex 的原生体验去适配，包括 Responses API、模型目录、凭证隔离、Reasoning level，以及安装后的 doctor 和 rollback。

我挺喜欢这个思路：Codex 这个 Harness 保留下来，底层用哪个模型可以更自由。

项目：
https://t.co/wOoq2uYKbL

reviewedPosts.text:
The most dangerous document extraction failure isn't a wrong value. It's a missing row that looks like nothing is wrong.

We released ExtractBench yesterday: 370 enterprise docs, 14 systems. The hardest test: long-list completeness. An unclaimed-property list with 26,725 rows. A creditor matrix with 8,624 records. A 13F with 3,063 holdings.

Frontier VLMs don't misread these docs, they abandon them. Precision stays high, recall collapses: 8.9–35.8% F1 on the longest documents. Every row they return looks correct, so spot checks pass while most of the document never came back.

Our new Extract tier, Agentic Plus, processes long docs iteratively instead of one pass: 96.1% F1 on long-list tasks, and the only system that holds flat as docs get longer.

Learn more about ExtractBench below👇

Paper: https://t.co/CmYy7Flrwu
